source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo — Subsidiaries' annual reports (incl. VUB Banka SK)
why_relevant: Parent-hosted, year-filterable archive (2007 onwards) of the full statutory annual reports of Intesa's international subsidiaries, with Vseobecna uverova banka (Slovakia) confirmed present. Gives a stable, long-history, one-URL-per-year path to VUB's audited accounts in English without depending on the Slovak site.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Group Annual Report (consolidated, incl. International Subsidiary Banks division)
why_relevant: The consolidated annual/interim reports carry the International Subsidiary Banks Division breakdown where VUB Slovakia appears as a reporting line (revenues, costs, loans, deposits, cost of risk) on a comparable basis with Hungary, Serbia, Slovenia, etc. — enabling cross-CEE benchmarking of the Slovak unit.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo — Investor Relations press releases archive
why_relevant: Deep archive (verified items back to 2002 referencing VUB) of parent statements on the Slovak unit — capital injections, stake changes, governance, strategic plans. Useful for reconstructing ownership and strategy history of VUB.

source_name: KBC Group Annual Report (consolidated, jvs-yyyy series)
why_relevant: Annual consolidated report with segment note and country detail for Slovakia (CSOB SK banking, insurance, leasing, asset management), plus risk, capital and ESG disclosures at subsidiary granularity.

source_name: KBC Group M&A / transaction disclosures on Slovakia (365.bank, OTP Banka Slovensko)
why_relevant: Parent is the disclosing party for structural change in the SK market: acquisition of ~98.45% of 365.bank (announced) and the earlier ~99.44% acquisition of OTP Banka Slovensko (effective Nov 2020). These filings carry deal rationale, consideration, market-share and integration detail found nowhere in local statutory filings.

source_name: Raiffeisen Bank International — Results & Reports hub
why_relevant: Index for RBI's interim/annual reports and the accompanying results files; RBI reports Slovakia as a separate country/segment line (Tatra banka) covering result, loans/deposits, NPE ratio, business outlets and staff. Primary parent channel for the #3 SK bank.

source_name: RBI quarterly 'Results Internet' workbook (XLSM)
why_relevant: Machine-readable quarterly results workbook accompanying the RBI interim report — the tabular route to Tatra banka / Slovakia country-segment figures without PDF table extraction. Macro-enabled Excel, so sandbox on ingest.

source_name: RBI Raiffeisen blog — market trends / country commentary on Slovakia
why_relevant: Parent-group research/commentary specifically on the Slovak financial market (structure, challenges, outlook, bank levy). Qualitative context that frames the quantitative segment data and signals the parent's strategic read of SK.

source_name: Tatra banka annual reports archive (EN, group-aligned)
why_relevant: English-language statutory annual reports of the RBI subsidiary, published on a stable /files/archiv/ path going back a decade-plus. Needed to reconcile RBI's country-segment (management view) numbers with Tatra banka's statutory IFRS accounts — the two rarely match exactly.

source_name: J&T FINANCE GROUP SE — consolidated annual report (vyrocni zprava)
why_relevant: Parent holding of J&T Banka and (until the KBC deal) 365.bank; its consolidated annual report breaks out subsidiary contributions (J&T Banka EUR 250m, 365.bank EUR 70m of a EUR 338m 2024 group profit) and Slovak bond-arranging volumes. The only consolidated view of the largest domestically-controlled SK banking group.

source_name: J&T Banka SK — zverejňované informácie / tlačové správy
why_relevant: Slovak-language disclosure and press channel of the J&T group's SK arm, incl. the /files/archiv/zverejnovane-informacie/ document folder holding consolidated annual reports and Pillar-3-style disclosures. Key for the J&T / 365.bank / Postova banka cluster where no listed-parent IR site exists.

source_name: PPF Group — annual accounts / annual reports
why_relevant: PPF's audited group annual accounts disclose the financial-services portfolio (PPF banka, Air Bank, Home Credit CZ/SK, Yettel Bank, ClearBank) and material transactions; Home Credit Slovakia (operating since 1999) is the consumer-finance channel relevant to SK payments/lending market structure. Confirms which entities remain in scope after divestments.

source_name: PPF Financial Holdings — annual report (bank/consumer-finance sub-holding)
why_relevant: The regulated financial sub-holding level, where Home Credit's country-by-country operations (incl. Slovakia) are reported with loan books, funding and risk metrics — closer to bank-comparable granularity than the top PPF group accounts.

source_name: UniCredit Bank Czech Republic and Slovakia — Debt Investor Relations
why_relevant: Slovakia is served by a Czech-domiciled UniCredit entity operating through an organisational unit (pobocka zahranicnej banky) since Dec 2013, so there is no separate SK statutory bank. This debt-IR page (prospectuses, covered-bond notices, annual and half-year reports) is therefore the principal disclosure channel for UniCredit's Slovak business.

source_name: UniCredit Group Investor Relations (CEE division reporting)
why_relevant: Top parent IR: quarterly results presentations and databooks with a Central Europe division view. Slovakia is normally folded into the Czech Republic & Slovakia country line, so this is the source that defines how visible (or invisible) SK is in UniCredit's group reporting.

source_name: Slovenská sporiteľňa — Financial indicators / investors page (subsidiary mirror of parent disclosure)
why_relevant: Publishes the SK-only figures that the parent aggregates (e.g. H1 2026 NII EUR 347.7m, +12.7% y/y; net fee income EUR 132.9m, +10.0%), released in step with Erste's group results. Serves as the reconciliation anchor for the Erste Slovakia segment and as a same-day cross-check on parent numbers.

source_name: VÚB Banka — annual reports document path (parent-aligned, EN/SK)
why_relevant: SK-side publication of the same VUB annual accounts Intesa hosts, plus covered-bond (kryté dlhopisy) financial information used by debt investors. Needed both as a mirror (in case the Intesa archive lags) and for Slovak-language governance/board sections not in the English edition.

source_name: Prague Stock Exchange (PSE) issuer report archive — foreign bank issuers incl. Erste Group Bank AG
why_relevant: Exchange-hosted FTP archive of annual reports filed by dual-listed issuers (Erste Group Bank AG confirmed present). A stable, non-bot-defended mirror for historical parent reports when corporate IR sites reorganise their URLs — a genuine archival fallback channel.

source_name: Finsider.sk (F Press s.r.o.) — Biznis / Spravy sections
why_relevant: Specialist Slovak financial news site that publishes a dedicated article for essentially every Slovak bank results release (quarterly and full-year), naming net profit, net interest income, fee income and loan volumes. Article dates act as a reliable date-stamp for when a disclosure went public, which is useful for change detection against bank IR pages.

source_name: SITA — Vo financiách (sita.sk/vofinanciach)
why_relevant: Slovak private news wire; its finance vertical carries bank results stories on results day, often near-verbatim renderings of the bank's Slovak press release, including figures for banks that publish no English release. SITA also maintains per-company tag pages (e.g. Tatra banka) that work as a chronological archive of that bank's disclosures.

source_name: TASR — Tlačová agentúra Slovenskej republiky
why_relevant: State news agency and the default carrier of Slovak corporate and NBS press releases. Also runs live streams of NBS press conferences (e.g. Ekonomický a menový vývoj), which are primary-adjacent events that precede bank-sector commentary in the rest of the media.

source_name: Teraz.sk — Ekonomika (TASR consumer portal)
why_relevant: Free, full-text public outlet for TASR wire copy. In practice this is the cheapest way to read TASR bank-results and NBS-statistics depeše without a wire licence, with stable dated article URLs suitable for change detection.

source_name: Forbes Slovensko — banking coverage and TOP 50 firiem ranking
why_relevant: Covers Slovak bank aggregate profitability (NBS-derived sector totals) and individual bank results, and separately maintains a structured company ranking (Rebríček Top 50 firiem Slovenska) with per-company profile pages including banks — a semi-structured dataset of revenue/profit that is easier to parse than prose articles.

source_name: Denník E (economic desk of Denník N)
why_relevant: Analytical economic desk with a recurring 'Graf dňa' format that visualises Slovak bank profitability and cross-EU comparisons, and strong coverage of the bank levy / transaction-tax policy debate — directly relevant to payments economics. Also runs a topic feed 'Banky a poisťovne' on the Denník N minute-by-minute stream.

source_name: Trend.sk — financie / banky section (TREND business weekly)
why_relevant: The main Slovak business weekly; historically the reference outlet for bank results commentary, executive interviews and bank-market rankings. Named directly in this coverage cell. Treat as high-value but access-constrained.

source_name: Hospodárske noviny / HNonline.sk (finweb finance vertical)
why_relevant: Slovakia's business daily; its Finweb vertical is a standing finance/banking news channel and a named target of this cell. Expected to carry results-day stories and CEO commentary.

source_name: Index — business desk of SME (sme.sk/index), per-company tag pages
why_relevant: Index is SME's business vertical and maintains per-company tag pages (confirmed for Tatra banka) that aggregate every article about a given bank chronologically — an efficient per-actor monitoring endpoint rather than a whole-site crawl.

source_name: oPeniazoch.sk (openiazoch.zoznam.sk)
why_relevant: Long-running Slovak personal-finance and markets portal that publishes bank sector profit aggregates (NBS-based) and individual results summaries. Free access makes it a good redundancy channel when Trend/HN/Denník E are paywalled.
